text:
ana: Heads-up — ran into a confusing UI case in Console's YAML editor. Schema lints are shown in the right-side preflight panel, but inline error underlines/gutters in the editor are missing. Users see a red bar on save and assume the entire save failed.

mike_r: ugh, yeah that's been a recurring complaint from a couple of SRE teams. They expect the editor to act like VSCode with inline squiggles.

jessica: curious — is this a parsing failure or a lint rule? We currently only show parse errors inline, and lint findings go to the preflight.

zana: it's mostly lint-level warnings (invalid header weighting, ambiguous regex) but in one case the linter suggested an autofix that would've changed semantics; user got spooked because they couldn't tell which line triggered the right-panel message.

mike_r: do we have a consistent mapping between preflight items and editor locations? If not, that's the bug. We should add a link-to-line for every preflight entry at least.

jessica: we do map when the analyzer can provide span info, but many of our rules currently return only 'path' in the config tree, not exact line/col. The YAML parser we use can also provide line numbers but we haven't integrated that for all lint checks.

zach: proposal: two small UX changes that are low-risk: 1) gutter icons for preflight errors with hover text and clickable to jump to preflight item, 2) inline faded markers for lint severity (warning/info) and solid underline for parse errors.

ana (typo) — that's me (should be ana), ignore above.

linter-bot: [automated] Preflight scan complete: 3 warnings, 1 suggestion. Warnings: header-weighting-conflict (no span), regex-inefficient (span: routes[3].match.headers[1]), duplicate-route-suspect (no span). Suggestion: normalize-quotes (autofix available).

devex_jen: small note — when autofix is available we currently show an 'Apply autofix' button in preflight. If we add inline underlines for lints, we should also show the quick-fix action (like a little lightning icon) inline to keep parity with the preflight affordance.

mike_r: agree. Also need to decide how strict mode works: should inline errors block save? Right now parse errors block, lints do not. If inline lints appear users will expect save-blocking for 'errors' but maybe not for 'warnings'.

jessica: recommend: keep current semantics — only parse errors block save. Introduce severity levels: error (blocks save + red underline), warn (yellow underline, does not block), info (blue dot). Autofix suggested actions can propose elevated severity if the fix would change semantics.

zach: implementation note: to render inline positions reliably we need to emit line/col from the lint pipeline. I'll add span extraction in the analyzer; might be ~2d of work + tests. We'll need to update telemetry to record which inline markers users click/accept autofix on.

ana again — sorry.

devex_jen: for telemetry, event names: console.yaml.inline_marker.clicked, console.yaml.autofix.accepted, console.yaml.preflight.opened. Track rule_id and span. Keep payload small.

jessica: tests: 1) unit: linter rules produce spans for common cases, 2) integration: editor highlights match preflight entries and jumping works, 3) e2e: autosave + save-blocking behavior when parse error present. Add a flaky test guard for race on autosave.

mike_r: ux copy question: what do we show in the gutter for rules without spans? Maybe a light-bulb at top-right that indicates '3 preflight items with no location' and clicking opens the panel.

zach: yes, don't invent line numbers for no-span rules. Show them in preflight list with `View details` and `Request span` action (which logs a telemetry event so we can prioritize rules missing spans).

ana: action items — zach to prototype span extraction + gutter markers (2d), jessica to spec severity mapping + tests (1d), devex_jen to add telemetry events & mapping (1d), mike_r to update product notes and copy for gutter/hint (0.5d). I'll follow up with PR link when ready.

linter-bot: [automated] Next preflight run scheduled in 1h.

mike_r: thanks — this should make Console less confusing for power users and reduce support tickets. :thumbsup:
